name: Al Taif Data Center
notes: ResearchAndMarkets/Arizton portfolio notices name Al Taif Data Center as an example covered by the Saudi existing/upcoming colocation database, but the public notice does not disclose operator, address, MW, tier, or operating date. Targeted searches did not surface a primary operator page, so status and capacity are left unknown.
Targeted searches for Ghran/Ghiran with data center, datacenter, cloud, hosting, hyperscale, Center3, STC, Mobily, GDH, and operator names found no public facility or project in this locality.

name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Saudi Arabia West (Jeddah) region
notes: Oracle release notes say the Jeddah OCI region me-jeddah-1 became available on 2020-02-01 with one availability domain. Oracle's Riyadh region page and public cloud region list continue to identify Saudi Arabia West (Jeddah) as an active public cloud region.

name: Center3 MENA Gateway 1 (MG1)
notes: Submarine Networks describes MG1 as a Tier IV data center in Jeddah owned and operated by STC. DataCenterMap lists MENA Gateway 1 by Center3 near Jeddah, while Center3 describes its STC-origin data-center and subsea-cable platform.

name: Center3 Jeddah203
notes: Baxtel lists Center3 Jeddah203 as a 150,000 sq ft carrier-neutral Tier III facility in Al-Idhaah near MG1 and JEDIX. MarkNtel's Saudi market page names Center3 Jeddah203 among key market facilities. Primary Center3 pages confirm Jeddah data centers but do not publish this site's capacity.

name: Center3 MENA Gateway 2
notes: OCOLO lists Center3 Jeddah MENA Gateway 2 in Jeddah with 9.60 MW power capacity. Center3 confirms a Jeddah footprint; DCD reports Center3's broader capacity expansion target but not MG2-specific MW.

name: Mobily Jeddah Fayhaa and Obhur data centers
notes: Mobily's official colocation service page says it operates strategically located Saudi data centers including Jeddah. DCD reports Mobily lists two operating Jeddah sites, Fayhaa and Obhur, as part of eight operating facilities; DataCenterPlatform lists a Mobily Jeddah location in Al Faiha District.

name: Gulf Data Hub KAUST 1
developer: Gulf Data Hub / Data Hub Tech at KAUST
notes: KAUST announced the 2017 groundbreaking for Gulf Data Hub's carrier-neutral data center at KAUST in Thuwal, within Jeddah Governorate. DataCenterMap lists Gulf Data Hub KAUST 1 at KAUST Research and Technology Park with 8 MW fully built-out power; ECG describes the Tier III KAUST data center complex.

name: Desert Dragon Jeddah facility
developer: ICS Arabia / Lumaotong Group / China Mobile International
notes: ICS Arabia's Desert Dragon page lists Jeddah phases targeted for Dec 2026 and Dec 2027. DCD reports construction began on the 187 MW Saudi cluster in October 2024; Goalfore/Saudi Gazette-derived coverage says the second phase is a 50 MW Jeddah data center planned to start construction in February 2025 and operate in Q4 2026.
Targeted searches for Khulays/Khulais with data center, datacenter, cloud, hosting, hyperscale, Center3, STC, Mobily, GDH, and operator names found no public facility or project in this governorate.

name: Center3 Shariya Makkah / NEIDC Makkah34
notes: DataCenterMap lists Center3 Shariya Makkah in Mecca with site code MKK1 / MKDC-34; OCOLO lists the same Center3 Mecca NEIDC Makkah34 facility. Center3 confirms Saudi data-center operations, but no public MW capacity was found for this site.

name: KAEC digital infrastructure hub: EDGNEX data center and Cinturion cable landing station
developer: EDGNEX Data Centers by DAMAC / Salam / Cinturion / Emaar The Economic City
notes: KAEC's 2023 announcement says Salam, EDGNEX, Cinturion, and Emaar The Economic City signed to make KAEC a digital infrastructure hub. DCD says EDGNEX would develop a data center and Cinturion a cable landing station outside Jeddah in KAEC. Public sources did not disclose KAEC-specific MW, separate from EDGNEX's Riyadh/Dammam capacity program.

name: Saudi National Bank Tier IV Data and Archive Center, King Abdullah Economic City
developer: Saudi National Bank / National Commercial Bank
notes: OCC Weavers' project page describes a completed Tier IV data centre and archive building delivered for National Commercial Bank, now Saudi National Bank, in King Abdullah Economic City. Capacity and original completion date were not published on the accessible page.
